newsitem.title: USA: DC losing millions in outdated personel procedures.
newsitem.headline: DC losing millions in outdated personel procedures.

text.p: The financially stressed District of Columbia is wasting up to $5.8 million annually because of antiquated methods of keeping tabs on employee attendance and time sheets, the city's inspector general said on Friday.
Currently the city manually keeps time for and distributes checks to its employees, which consumes 400,000 to 500,000 hours each year, Angela Avant said following a review by her office.
The process also is "subject to fraud, mismanagement and waste because employees and supervisors are not held accountable for the accuracy of their time," Avant said.
Avant said the city could save millions simply by requiring each employee to record and report time worked and having supervisors review and approve reports.
